newsitem.title: GERMANY: New gap opens in German defence budget.
newsitem.headline: New gap opens in German defence budget.

text.p: Payment delays and the cost of sending troops to Bosnia could add up to two billion marks next year to Germany's already strained military budget, the Defence Ministry said on Thursday.

The ministry statement confirmed a report in Die Welt newspaper which revealed the overshoot -- likely to complicate Finance Minister Theo Waigel's bid this week to bring down the budget deficit to qualify for European monetary union.
"An already foreseeable burden on the 1997 budget totalling between 1.5 and two billion marks is not unrealistic," the ministry said.
Unpaid bills which will have to be met next year total 800 million marks, a spokesman said.

The Defence Ministry will have to pay 300 million marks for its involvement this year in the IFOR peacekeeping force in Bosnia. Costs of committing troops to a possible follow-up operation are likely to total 400 million marks.
Under pressure to reduce military spending, Defence Minister Volker Ruehe agreed reluctantly last summer to cut the defence budget back to 46.5 billion marks next year.

Now Waigel is asking all ministries to contribute to savings of three billion marks he wants to agree by next week -- but has said that procurement plans for the four-country Eurofighter combat aircraft should be spared from the cuts.

However, Die Welt said Ruehe had told a confidential meeting of parliament's defence committee that the 392 million marks sought by the Eurofighter consortium next year to begin serial production would not be available.
The Eurofighter is being built by Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, British Aerospace, Italy's Alenia ALEI.RO, and Spain's Casa.
